## Why? {#why}

**Research question:** Do older drivers react more slowly to a takeover request? And is the usability rating related to trust in the system?

A correlation describes how closely two variables are related; a regression says how much the outcome changes per unit of the predictor, in the unit of measurement (ms, SUS points). Both need independent observations: with repeated measures, summarise per person first.

## Concept {#concept}

```{=html}
<figure class="rt-figure">
<svg viewBox="0 0 560 220" role="img" aria-labelledby="fig-rg-title fig-rg-desc" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <title id="fig-rg-title">Intercept and slope of a regression line</title>
  <desc id="fig-rg-desc">Coordinate system with age in decades from 40 on the x axis and reaction time on the y axis. A rising line crosses the vertical line at age10 equal to 0 at the intercept. A step triangle shows the slope: one unit to the right, b milliseconds up.</desc>
  <line x1="60" y1="190" x2="540" y2="190" class="rt-fig-axis" />
  <line x1="60" y1="190" x2="60" y2="20" class="rt-fig-axis" />
  <line x1="220" y1="190" x2="220" y2="25" class="rt-fig-mean" />
  <line x1="70" y1="150" x2="530" y2="60" class="rt-fig-a" />
  <line x1="220" y1="120.7" x2="340" y2="120.7" class="rt-fig-arrow" />
  <line x1="340" y1="120.7" x2="340" y2="97.2" class="rt-fig-arrow" />
  <text x="220" y="208" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label">0 (= 40 years)</text>
  <text x="340" y="208" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label">1 (= 50 years)</text>
  <text x="530" y="208" text-anchor="end" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">age10</text>
  <text x="70" y="30" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">rt_ms</text>
  <text x="228" y="140" class="rt-fig-label">intercept</text>
  <text x="348" y="114" class="rt-fig-label">slope b</text>
  <text x="280" y="114" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">+1</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The intercept is the expected value at predictor = 0, the slope the change per unit. Centring moves 0 to a meaningful place.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

- **Correlation** `correlation::correlation()`: r from −1 to 1 with 95% CI, t, df and p in one table. r² is the share of common variance.
- **Regression** `lm(outcome ~ predictor, data = ...)`, read with `parameters::model_parameters()`: coefficient, CI, t, df, p.
- **Centring and scaling:** transform predictors so that 0 is a meaningful value and one unit is a meaningful size (`age10 = (age - 40) / 10`). Calculations belong in `mutate()`, not in the formula.
- **Factors as predictors:** the first level is the reference; each coefficient is the difference of one level from it.
- **Model fit** `performance::r2()`: share of explained variance.
- **Association is not causation:** only randomly assigned conditions can be interpreted causally.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## More: correlation and regression are related

- With one predictor, t and p of the slope and of the correlation are identical.
- The standardised slope (both variables in SD units) is r.
- Regression has the advantage of units: "27 ms per decade" is more tangible than "r = .28", and further predictors can be added.
- `correlation()` adjusts p for several correlations with Holm (`p_adjust`); for a single correlation this changes nothing.
:::

## Example {#example}

Prepare the SUS score and the trust score (as in the lesson "Questionnaires and scales"):

```{webr}
scored <- survey |>
  filter(attention_check == 4) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(sus_01, sus_03, sus_05, sus_07, sus_09), \(x) x - 1),
    across(c(sus_02, sus_04, sus_06, sus_08, sus_10), \(x) 5 - x),
    sus = 25 * rowMeans(pick(sus_01:sus_10), na.rm = TRUE),
    across(c(trust_3, trust_5), \(x) 8 - x),
    trust = row_means(pick(trust_1:trust_6), min_valid = 5)
  )

scored |>
  select(sus, trust) |>
  correlation()
```

How many more SUS points per point of trust? And how much variance does that explain?

```{webr}
fit <- lm(sus ~ trust, data = scored)
model_parameters(fit)
r2(fit)
```

**How to report it:** SUS score and trust were clearly related, r = .48, 95% CI [.35, .59], p < .001. Per point of trust (scale 1–7), the SUS score was 9.1 points higher, 95% CI [6.4, 11.8]; the model explains 23% of the variance. Whether trust influences the rating or the other way round, the survey leaves open.

## Package comparison {#packages}

| Task | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Correlation with CI | **correlation** `correlation()` (table, several pairs, Holm correction) | `cor.test()`: one pair, list instead of table; `cor()`: only r, no CI |
| Regression results | **parameters** `model_parameters()` | `summary(fit)` with `confint(fit)`: standard in other people's code; `broom::tidy(conf.int = TRUE)` |
| Model fit | **performance** `r2()`, `model_performance()` | `summary(fit)$r.squared` |
| Centring | **dplyr** `mutate(age10 = (age - 40) / 10)` | `datawizard::center()`, `standardize()`: at the mean or in SD units |

## Cheat sheet {#cheatsheet}

```r
# one row per person first
rt_by_person <- driving_sim |>
  summarise(rt_ms = mean(rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(participant, age))

# correlation with CI
rt_by_person |> select(age, rt_ms) |> correlation()

# regression with a centred, scaled predictor
rt_age <- rt_by_person |> mutate(age10 = (age - 40) / 10)
fit <- lm(rt_ms ~ age10, data = rt_age)
model_parameters(fit)
r2(fit)

# factor as predictor: reference = first level
lm(sus ~ interface + tech_affinity, data = scored)
```

- Clarify the unit first, then correlate.
- CI instead of only p: which values are compatible with the data?
- Prepare predictors with `mutate()`, do not calculate in the formula.
- Intercept = expected value at predictor 0 or in the reference level.
